headline: USD is stronger today, with EUR/USD near two-month lows.
summary: Markets had already priced in rate hikes from both the Fed (Sept 16, to 3.75-4.00%) and the ECB (Sept 10, to 2.50%), both citing energy-driven inflation from the ongoing Middle East conflict. Since those decisions, stronger-than-expected US economic data (PMI surveys) and hawkish comments from Fed officials have pushed the dollar higher, even though eurozone business activity has also been surprisingly strong. As a result, EUR/USD has slid from around 1.15 in mid-September to roughly 1.138 now, near its weakest level in about two months.

forYou: With the dollar relatively strong right now, converting USD paychecks into euros gets you somewhat fewer euros than it did a couple of weeks ago.
